title: Defying Gravity - Kevin Hou, Google DeepMind
talk_summary: Kevin Hou presents Google Antigravity, an agent-first IDE with three surfaces (editor, agent-controlled browser, agent manager) built around 'artifacts'—dynamic, model-chosen representations (plans, task lists, walkthroughs, screen recordings) that replace raw chain-of-thought for supervision. He argues the product is powered by a research-product flywheel where internal usage surfaces model gaps that feed back to model teams.

takeaways.technique: Artifact-based review instead of transcript review
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents emit structured artifacts (plan/PRD with open questions, task list, architecture diagram, end-of-task walkthrough like a PR description) so humans review a compact visual summary rather than scrolling token streams.

An agent-controlled Chrome clicks through the running app and produces a screen recording plus DOM access, so verification is behavioral, not just a diff; the multimodal model then iterates on that recording.
takeaways.evidence_quote: instead of showing you a diff of what I did, let's instead show you a recording of Chrome... you get verifiable results

takeaways.technique: Plan artifact with surfaced open questions and auto-continue
takeaways.what_they_do: Before executing, the agent writes a plan/PRD and lists open questions; it auto-continues only if there are none, otherwise it blocks for answers.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it'll surface, hey, you should probably answer these three questions before I get going... the model will decide whether or not it can auto continue

takeaways.technique: Artifacts as shared memory across agents/subagents
takeaways.what_they_do: Artifacts carry metadata on who should see them (subagents, other conversations, memory bank), so derived knowledge like an API schema report is persisted and reused instead of re-derived.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You wouldn't want to just throw that away and have to rederive it the second time... it'll store it in your memory

takeaways.what_they_do: A single agent-manager inbox surfaces only items needing human attention (e.g., risky terminal commands) with OS notifications, enabling one person to supervise many parallel agents.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it lets you manage many agents at once... things that require your attention... One click, you can manage many different things happening at once

takeaways.what_they_do: The team uses its own product internally so real usage exposes model/harness gaps that feed back into training and tool fixes, complementing offline evals.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it gives you this level of insight that eval just simply can't give you
